Short Description: Ancient temple complex dedicated to Lord Shiva and Nath sect master Gorakhnath with a sacred pond where large crowds gather during Mahashivratri.

Alternate Name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
Short Description: Historic 17th-century gurdwara sanctified by the personal visit of the Ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, in 1670 CE; preserves historical hand-written Hukamnamas and sacred relic cot.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Important pilgrimage shrine on the official Bihar Sikh Circuit.
Primary Source: Bihar Tourism Sikh Circuit (tourism.bihar.gov.in) & District Administration Katihar

Short Description: Historic Ganga riverfront town where Swami Vivekananda halted, and where river ferry links Bihar to Jharkhand; mythological association with Lord Krishna losing his jewel (Mani).

Short Description: Rare heritage temple where an unbroken sacred Vedic fire (Akhand Agnihotra) has been maintained continuously for over a century by generations of Agnihotri priests.

Approximate Location: Dhamhara Ghat / Mansi block, 12 km from Khagaria
Short Description: Revered ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Katyayani (sixth form of Navadurga) situated at the confluence of Kosi and Bagmati rivers, drawing millions of pilgrims from Kosi and Mithila regions.

Short Description: Spectacular water landscape where the energetic Kosi and Bagmati rivers meet before joining the Ganga, famous for flood ecology and sunset viewpoints.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Scenic river geography landmark.

Approximate Location: Bandarjhula, Dighalbank block, on Indo-Nepal border
Short Description: Ancient Krishna temple on the Mechi riverbank where ancient black stone sculptures and Mauryan-era artifacts were excavated.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of National Importance in Bihar.

Short Description: Historic estate palace of the Nawabs of Khagra and site of the annual Khagra Mela, established in 1883, historically the second largest cattle and trade fair in the subcontinent.

Short Description: Over 15,000 acres of lush undulating green tea plantations situated in the foothills of the Himalayas bordering West Bengal and Nepal; Bihar's only tea producing district.

Short Description: Picturesque riverfront with walking promenade along the fast-flowing Mahananda river, ideal for morning walks and bird watching.

Short Description: Celebrated regional temple of Goddess Jagdamba (Maharani Sthan) established over 500 years ago, famous for community faith and massive Chhath congregations.

Short Description: Picturesque natural perennial water spring, deep forested gorge, and ancient cave associated with Sage Rishyashringa (who officiated King Dasharatha's Putrakameshti Yajna in Ramayana).

Short Description: Ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Kali/Dakini, surrounded by natural ponds and associated with regional tantric lore.

Short Description: Ancient Shiva temple mentioned in Varaha Purana as the place where Sage Rishyashringa meditated; houses a sacred self-manifested lingam and host to one of Bihar's largest month-long Mahashivratri Melas.

Short Description: Sacred temple commemorating the legend of Mahakavi Vidyapati, where Lord Shiva worked as a servant named Ugna to serve his devotee poet until revealed at this site.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Celebrated Mithila cultural and poetic heritage site.

Short Description: Over 40-km long colossal stone defensive wall built of massive unworked boulders without mortar, dating to the 6th century BCE (pre-Mauryan Haryanka dynasty).

Short Description: Imposing quadrangular fortified citadel built in 1722 by Saif Khan, the Mughal Nawab of Purnia, featuring high stone ramparts, rounded bastions, and battlements on the old Kosi course.

Short Description: Former historic colonial estate and indigo planter's bungalow transformed into a 25-acre landscaped eco-park with boating lake, hanging suspension bridge, and children's amusement zones.

Short Description: Impregnable 16th-century hill fort built by Sher Shah Suri, famous for its hidden underground multi-level tunnels, palace ruins, and sheer defensive cliff drops into Durgavati river.

Short Description: Sacred site on the bank of Sarayu river identified as the hermitage of Maharshi Gautama, where Lord Rama redeemed Ahilya; venue of the traditional Godna mela on Kartik Purnima.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Official Ramayana Circuit destination in western Bihar.

Subcategory: Ancient Fortified River Port / ASI Monument
Approximate Location: Manjhi, on the bank of Ghaghara river
Short Description: Extensive brick ramparts and fortifications of an ancient riverine port and city dating to Mauryan and Kushan epochs.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of National Importance.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #51)

Short Description: Ancient temple associated with mythological lore of Narada Muni's penance; major regional pilgrimage hub with massive annual Shravani and Shivratri congregation.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Featured place of religious interest on saran.nic.in.

Subcategory: Sacred Confluence Temple & Asia's Largest Cattle Fair
Approximate Location: Sonepur, at the confluence of Gandak and Ganga
Short Description: Sacred temple dedicated to Lord Harihar (Vishnu and Shiva unified), venue of the month-long Sonepur Mela (Asia's largest cattle and cultural fair) held every Kartik Purnima.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Globally celebrated cultural festival and premier pilgrimage stop on Bihar Tourism calendar.

Short Description: Historic water reservoir built during medieval times, surrounded by masonry ghats and used as the principal venue for Chhath festival.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Documented place of civic and cultural heritage on sheikhpura.nic.in.

Short Description: Picturesque isolated hill rising 500 feet above the plains with an ancient temple of Lord Shiva on the summit, offering breathtaking 360-degree views of Sheikhpura town and countryside.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Most popular scenic and spiritual destination on sheikhpura.nic.in.

Subcategory: Colossal Pala Vishnu Monolith / Archaeological Site
Short Description: Houses a magnificent 7.5-foot monolithic black basalt stone statue of Lord Vishnu from the Pala era (10th century CE), unearthed during canal excavation in 1992, with carvings of Dasavatara.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Prime religious and archaeological landmark in Sheikhpura district, drawing pilgrims from all over Bihar.

Approximate Location: Dekuli, Piprarhi block, 7 km from Sheohar
Short Description: Venerated ancient Shiva temple surrounded by holy water tanks, believed to date to the Dvapara Yuga and founded by Dronacharya / Pandavas; major venue of Shravani Mela.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Foremost cultural and spiritual pilgrimage destination in Sheohar district, officially highlighted on sheohar.nic.in.

Short Description: Heritage residence and courtyards of the historic Sheohar Raj estate, displaying classical colonial and northern Bihar zamindari architectural styles.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Primary historical landmark of Sheohar town.

Short Description: Sprawling peaceful spiritual ashram with 108 residential prayer rooms, ornate temples, and lush gardens, serving as a center of Ramayana study.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Prominent cultural retreat in eastern Sitamarhi.

Short Description: Ancient Shiva temple said to have been founded by King Videha (Janaka) during the Putrakameshti Yajna prior to the birth of Sita.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Important Ramayana Circuit shrine officially documented on sitamarhi.nic.in.

Short Description: Historic temple complex dedicated to Goddess Sita, Lord Rama, and Lakshmana, with Janaki Kund holy tank; major pilgrimage site during Ram Navami and Vivaha Panchami.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Foremost cultural symbol of Sitamarhi district.
Duplicate / Conflict Notes: Already in HiddenYatra as place ID 25.

Approximate Location: Bairgania road, 8 km north-east of Sitamarhi
Short Description: Venerable centuries-old banyan tree where the bridal palanquin carrying Goddess Sita and Lord Rama is said to have halted for rest on their journey from Janakpur to Ayodhya.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Sacred living heritage monument on the Ramayana Circuit.
Primary Source: Bihar Tourism Ramayana Circuit (tourism.bihar.gov.in) & District Administration Sitamarhi

Subcategory: Officially Recognized Sita Birthplace / Central PRASAD Project
Approximate Location: Punaura village, 5 km west of Sitamarhi town
Short Description: Officially recognized divine birthplace of Goddess Sita, where King Janaka ploughed the golden furrow and the infant Sita emerged from an earthen pot; features Punaura Kund and grand park.
Why Tourism-Relevant: National flagship pilgrimage center under Government of India's PRASAD scheme, major stop on Ramayana Circuit.
Primary Source: Ministry of Tourism, Govt of India (PRASAD Scheme) & Bihar Tourism

Short Description: Memorial dedicated to 15-year-old student martyr Umakant Prasad Verma, who sacrificed his life hoisting the Indian Tricolor during the 1942 Quit India movement at Patna Secretariat.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Nationalist freedom movement pilgrimage site.

Approximate Location: Mehdar, Siswan block, 32 km south of Siwan
Short Description: Revered ancient Shiva temple built by King Mahendra of Nepal surrounded by an enormous 551-bigha sacred lake (Kamal Dah Sarovar) famous for healing lotus water and migratory birds.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Foremost religious pilgrimage site in Siwan district, officially featured on siwan.nic.in.

Approximate Location: Gutani block, on Bihar-UP border, Siwan
Short Description: Ancient temple housing a unique black stone Shiva lingam believed to have been worshipped by Banasura, with an eternal sulfur well.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Prominent border pilgrimage center officially documented on siwan.nic.in.

Subcategory: National Memorial / First President Birthplace / ASI
Approximate Location: Zeeradei, 13 km west of Siwan town
Short Description: Preserved ancestral house and memorial museum of Bharat Ratna Dr. Rajendra Prasad, independent India's first President and President of the Constituent Assembly, housing his personal books, bed, and photographs.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of profound national importance, visited by national leaders.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #52)

Short Description: Historic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, drawing devotees from across Supaul and neighboring Nepal during Shivratri and Shravani Mela.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Prominent religious destination officially highlighted on supaul.nic.in.

Approximate Location: Birpur, on Indo-Nepal border, northern Supaul
Short Description: Colossal 56-gate water barrage spanning 1,150 meters across the turbulent Kosi river on the international border, offering spectacular panoramic vistas of the river basin and Himalayan foothills.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Premier engineering landmark and scenic sunset tourism destination in Kosi division.

Short Description: Ancient temple with sacred stone lingam and large festival grounds.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Documented place of tourist interest on supaul.nic.in.

Subcategory: Complete Ashokan Pillar & Stupa / ASI Monument
Short Description: Spectacular 18.3-meter monolithic polished sandstone pillar erected by Emperor Ashoka with an intact crowned lion capital, facing north towards Kushinagar, accompanied by Stupa of Ananda and brick monasteries.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of National Importance.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #53)

Place Name: Baraila Lake / Salim Ali Jubba Sahni Sanctuary
Short Description: 198-hectare perennial wetland sanctuary designated by Bihar Government, winter host to over 59 species of migratory waterfowl and shorebirds.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Important avian eco-tourism and birdwatching reserve in Tirhut.
Primary Source: Bihar Forest Department & Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Short Description: Authentic 5th-century BCE mud-and-brick stupa built by the Licchavis to enshrine their 1/8th share of Lord Buddha's sacred cremation bone relics (excavated in 1958, relics in Patna Museum).
Why Tourism-Relevant: One of the most sacred Buddhist archaeological sites in existence, ASI Centrally Protected Monument.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #55)

Short Description: Traditional Shvetambara Jain holy site marking the exact birthplace of the 24th Tirthankara Lord Mahavira (born to King Siddhartha and Queen Trishala in 599 BCE), with commemorative memorial.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Foremost pilgrimage site on the global Jain Circuit.
Primary Source: Bihar Tourism Jain Circuit (tourism.bihar.gov.in) & Shvetambara Jain Mahasabha

Alternate Name: Kaal Bhairav Wooden Temple / Nepali Mandir
Short Description: Unique 18th-century pagoda-style wooden Hindu temple built by Nepalese military commander Mathabar Singh Thapa, featuring erotic wooden bracket carvings and Shiva shrine.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Bihar State Protected Monument, architectural marvel on the Gandak riverbank.
Primary Source: Bihar State Archaeology Directorate & District Administration Vaishali

Short Description: Enormous 1-km perimeter ancient fortified earth-and-brick mound believed to be the ancient parliament assembly hall (Sansthagara) where 7,707 Licchavi representatives assembled to govern the republic.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Birthplace of democratic governance, ASI Centrally Protected Monument.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #56)

Approximate Location: Vaishali village, 35 km north of Hajipur
Short Description: Seat of the ancient Licchavi republic (6th century BCE), the world's first documented democracy, where Lord Buddha gave his last sermon and courtesan Amrapali offered her mango grove.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Global heritage and Buddhist-Jain pilgrimage destination.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India & Bihar Tourism
Duplicate / Conflict Notes: Already in HiddenYatra as place ID 10.

Subcategory: White Marble Peace Pagoda & Lotus Pond
Short Description: Majestic white marble World Peace Pagoda consecrated in 1996 by Nipponzan Myohoji, housing four golden statues of Buddha depicting his birth, enlightenment, first sermon, and Mahaparinirvana.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Major landmark of international peace and Buddhist devotion.

Short Description: Grand 18th-century palace complex of the historic Bettiah Raj, one of the wealthiest aristocratic estates of Bihar, featuring Indo-Saracenic gates, temples, and audience halls.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Significant architectural and cultural landmark of Champaran.

Approximate Location: Bhitiharwa, Gaunaha block, 45 km from Bettiah
Short Description: Historic ashram and primary school founded by Mahatma Gandhi and Kasturba Gandhi on November 20, 1917 during the historic Champaran Satyagraha; preserves Gandhi's charkha, table, and original hut.
Why Tourism-Relevant: National freedom heritage monument and prime anchor of the official Gandhi Circuit in India.
Primary Source: Ministry of Culture, Govt of India & Gandhi Smriti Darshan Samiti

Short Description: Colossal 90-foot high ancient brick fortified mound dating to the Mauryan and Sunga eras, believed to be part of King Chanakya's or ancient regional ruler's defensive fortifications.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of National Importance.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #57)

Short Description: Massive 82-foot high ancient Buddhist brick stupa (one of the largest in India) and an intact 35-foot polished monolithic sandstone Ashokan column with crowned lion capital and edicts.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of supreme national archaeological importance.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #58, #59)

Subcategory: Twin Ashokan Pillar Sites / ASI Monument
Approximate Location: Rampurva, Gaunaha block, near Indo-Nepal border
Short Description: Site where Emperor Ashoka erected two magnificent pillars in 243 BCE; home of the famous Rampurva Bull Capital (now gracing the entrance of Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi) and Lion capital.
Why Tourism-Relevant: ASI Centrally Protected Monument of worldwide sculptural fame.
Primary Source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Patna Circle, Monument #63)

Subcategory: Highest Point in Bihar (2,884 ft) & Border Fort
Short Description: Highest geographical summit in Bihar (880 meters / 2,884 feet), offering breathtaking views of Himalayan snow-capped peaks (Annapurna, Dhaulagiri) and ruins of an ancient border fortress.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Top trekking, mountain viewpoint, and adventure destination in Bihar.
Primary Source: Bihar Forest Department & District Administration West Champaran

Short Description: Sacred confluence of Gandak, Panchanad, and Sonaha rivers with a breathtaking gorge where Maharshi Valmiki composed the epic Ramayana and Goddess Sita gave birth to Luv and Kush.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Supreme cultural and scenic pilgrimage destination on the Indo-Nepal border.
Primary Source: Bihar Tourism Ramayana Circuit (tourism.bihar.gov.in) & District Administration

Short Description: 8.87 sq km wildlife sanctuary encompassing an oxbow lake on the Gandak river floodplains, swamp forests, spotted deer, barking deer, wild boar, and wintering migratory waterbirds.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Important wetland and wildlife tourism sanctuary.
Primary Source: Bihar Forest Department & Ministry of Environment & Forests

Subcategory: National Park & Only Tiger Reserve in Bihar
Short Description: Sprawling 898 sq km Himalayan Terai biosphere reserve, Bihar's sole Tiger Reserve, home to 54+ Royal Bengal Tigers, Indian rhinoceros, leopards, wild dogs, and 241 bird species.
Why Tourism-Relevant: Flagship wildlife and eco-tourism destination of Bihar, bordering Chitwan National Park of Nepal.
Primary Source: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) & Bihar Forest Dept
